findings.evidenceJa: 五尺余もの長刀
findings.governingReading: Assassin effortlessly wields a blade more than five shaku long.
findings.explanation: The exceptional length establishing the weapon’s tactical burden disappears.

findings.evidenceJa: アサシンの長刀は疾風だった
findings.governingReading: Assassin’s long blade is likened to a swift gale against Saber’s lightning.
findings.explanation: A fast linear contrast becomes the much larger phenomenon “hurricane.”

findings.evidenceJa: しなやかな軌跡
findings.governingReading: The blade’s supple curved trajectory receives and redirects Saber’s blows.
findings.explanation: The English produces a nonsensical mechanical phrase and obscures the contrast in sword paths.

findings.highlight: easy to go inside on him
findings.evidenceJa: 懐に入るのは容易い
findings.governingReading: Once the long blade is handled, entering inside its effective reach should be easy.
findings.explanation: Malformed phrasing obscures the tactical meaning of closing within a long weapon’s reach.

findings.evidenceJa: 打ち込みも素晴らしい
findings.governingReading: Assassin praises the force and quality of Saber’s committed strikes.
findings.explanation: “Drive” turns a concrete sword action into a vague personal quality.

findings.highlight: There are no stances for that man
findings.evidenceJa: あの男には構えなどない
findings.governingReading: Assassin is not bound to a fixed ready stance and can cut from any posture.
findings.explanation: The English suggests that stances do not exist for him rather than describing his freedom from one.

findings.evidenceJa: いよし、当たりだ
findings.governingReading: Assassin confirms a blade-contact “hit” that lets him gauge the invisible sword.
findings.explanation: A tactile measurement cue becomes a generic declaration of correctness.

findings.highlight: That it is because of her invisible sword that she is able to block
findings.evidenceJa: 偏にこの剣のおかげなのだと
findings.governingReading: Saber knows she has defended this far solely because of the invisible sword.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the governing realization as a dependent-clause fragment.

findings.evidenceJa: 満足に打ち合ってもいない
findings.governingReading: They have not even exchanged enough full blows for a proper measurement.
findings.explanation: The English says they have not exchanged blows at all, contradicting the preceding dozens of clashes.

findings.highlight: if I fight off your sword
findings.evidenceJa: まともに打ち合わぬ
findings.governingReading: Assassin avoids meeting Saber’s blade head-on because his long sword would break.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes the unclear action “fight off your sword” for direct blade contact.

findings.evidenceJa: 剣を鞘に納めたまま戦とは
findings.governingReading: Assassin metaphorically accuses Saber of keeping her sword sheathed by holding back its power.
findings.explanation: The English presents a physical sheath as though it remains on the invisible blade.

findings.evidenceJa: 頭上の有利
findings.governingReading: Assassin gives up the advantage of occupying higher ground on the stairs.
findings.explanation: “Being overhead” misstates the spatial relation as vertical suspension.

findings.evidenceJa: それは事実だ
findings.governingReading: Saber’s instinct recognizes as fact that his descent has not made her safer.
findings.explanation: The English assigns a truth claim to Assassin instead of narrating her tactical realization.

findings.highlight: With Saber trying to charge in, Assassin stands ready.
findings.evidenceJa: それは。この戦いが始まって以来、見せた事もない剣士の構え
findings.governingReading: At less than three meters, Saber sees a true stance Assassin has never shown in the fight.
findings.explanation: The English inserts an extra charge and readying action before the source presents the unprecedented stance.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの剣戟を上回る速度
findings.governingReading: The descending strike is faster than Saber’s own sword blow.
findings.explanation: The English broadens a comparison between attacks into speed that overwhelms Saber herself.

findings.highlight: Saber trusts her instincts and rolls down the stone steps
findings.evidenceJa: 直感だけに任せて、セイバーは石段を転がり落ちた
findings.governingReading: At intuition’s warning, Saber abandons posture and tumbles down the steps in desperate escape.
findings.explanation: “Trusts” and “rolls” make the escape sound controlled and deliberate before the source stresses the lack of any breakfall.

findings.evidenceJa: 必死に体を倒し
findings.governingReading: Saber desperately throws her body down and keeps tumbling without checking her momentum.
findings.explanation: The English invents a spinning motion and softens the ugly physical desperation.

findings.highlight: something I thought of when considering how to hit swallows
findings.evidenceJa: 思いつき、身に付いただけ
findings.governingReading: Assassin says he conceived the aim of cutting a swallow and eventually acquired the technique.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the completed, acquired technique to a thought experiment about hitting swallows.

findings.evidenceJa: 燕を捕らえられぬ
findings.governingReading: A single linear sword path cannot catch and cut a swallow moving freely through the air.
findings.explanation: “Apprehend” imports the sense of arrest or intellectual grasp into the concrete sword problem.

findings.evidenceJa: 一念鬼神に通じる
findings.governingReading: Single-minded resolve is said to reach even gods and demons.
findings.explanation: A culturally charged proverb becomes a generic motivational slogan, weakening the impossible-human-feat framing.

findings.evidenceJa: 多重次元屈折現象
findings.governingReading: The written phenomenon term carries “Kischur Zelretch” as its imposed reading.
findings.explanation: The English separates base term and ruby into two adjacent labels, obscuring that one names the other.

findings.highlight: If everything is to happen at the same time, the second blow has to be slower
findings.evidenceJa: 全てが同時であるなら、[ruby text=二の太刀 o2o=1]円の軌跡はどうしても遅くなる
findings.governingReading: Both blades exist simultaneously, but the second curved path necessarily arrives later because it travels farther.
findings.explanation: The English says the second blow itself must be slower, breaking the distinction between simultaneous generation and unequal arrival time.

findings.evidenceJa: 生前では叶わなかった立ち会い
findings.governingReading: Assassin rejoices at receiving the duel he could not attain during life.
findings.explanation: The English removes the lifelong lack that makes being summoned worthwhile to him.

findings.highlight: battle someone I can fully use my secret attacks on
findings.evidenceJa: 存分に振舞える殺し合い
findings.governingReading: Assassin welcomes a fight to the death in which he can freely display his secret sword technique.
findings.explanation: A death match becomes a generic battle, and one sword technique becomes plural “attacks.”

findings.evidenceJa: 対応策がほとんどない
findings.governingReading: Knowing the technique still leaves almost no way to answer it.
findings.explanation: A near-total tactical limitation becomes an absolute impossibility.

findings.highlight: the large firm trees of the forest
findings.evidenceJa: 太く堅固な山門の木々
findings.governingReading: Even the thick, solid timbers of the temple gate shake and creak.
findings.explanation: The built wooden gate becomes living trees in a forest, changing the object and scale of the wind’s effect.

findings.highlight: would easily blow away a normal person
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の一人や二人などたやすく吹き飛ばす
findings.governingReading: The gale could readily blow away one or two human beings.
findings.explanation: The English loses the explicit number and adds an unsupported distinction of a “normal” person.

findings.evidenceJa: その合間
findings.governingReading: During the interval while released wind rages, Saber continues controlling it.
findings.explanation: A sustained interval becomes an instant, conflicting with the following estimate of several minutes.

findings.highlight: the commanding magic of the sword
findings.evidenceJa: 戒めの魔術
findings.governingReading: The spell laid upon the sword is a binding or restraint that controls the raging wind.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the conceptual emphasis from restraint to command and uses nonstandard technical wording.

findings.evidenceJa: 鎌首をもたげていた
findings.governingReading: The mass of wind rears its head like a serpent as it prepares to engulf Assassin.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the threat but removes the animating image.
